back: Prior P(B) before evidence; posterior P(B | A) after.

front: (HL) Law of total probability (the Bayes denominator)?
back: $P(A) = P(B)P(A\mid B) + P(B')P(A\mid B')$ — the sum over all branches of the tree that end in $A$.

front: (HL) Bayes' theorem for three mutually exclusive, exhaustive causes $B_1, B_2, B_3$?
back: $P(B_i\mid A) = \dfrac{P(B_i)P(A\mid B_i)}{P(B_1)P(A\mid B_1) + P(B_2)P(A\mid B_2) + P(B_3)P(A\mid B_3)}$.

front: (HL) 1% have a disease; the test detects 95% of cases and gives 5% false positives. P(disease | positive)?

back: No — that is $P(+\mid D)$. For a rare disease $P(D\mid +)$ can be much smaller, because most positives are false positives.
False positive: test positive without the condition, $P(+\mid D')$. False negative: test negative with it, $P(-\mid D)$.
First branches: causes (priors). Second: evidence given each cause. P(cause | evidence) = (path through that cause and the evidence) ÷ (sum of all paths to the evidence).

front: (HL) Machines A, B, C make 50%, 30%, 20% of items with defect rates 2%, 3%, 5%. P(C | defective)?
(HL) Is Bayes' theorem in the formula booklet?
back: Yes — both the two-event form (with $B$, $B'$) and the three-event form are given.
